title: GOD OF JEREMIAH MORNING PROPHETIC DECLARATION SPEAK YOUR FUTURE INTO EXISTENCE
text: Before you were born, before your mother knew she was carrying you, before the hospital, before the name, before the first cry, there was a meeting in heaven, and in that meeting your future was discussed, not guessed at, not hoped for, discussed, deliberated, agreed upon, decreed by a God who does not speculate, by a God who does not plan in pencil, by a God who writes in ink that no devil in hell has ever been able to erase. And what was decreed in that meeting is what you are about to hear today. Not what the enemy has been saying about your life, not what the circumstances have been suggesting, not what the delay has been implying, what God said. Before the world began, before the attack launched, before the detour started, what God said. And today we are going to align our mouths with that decree. We are going to speak what God wrote. >> [music] >> We are going to call into existence the future that heaven already confirmed. We are going to prophesy over ourselves the way Ezekiel prophesied over dry bones, and watch what was dead come back to life. But before the word goes one sentence further, I want you to share this message right now. Not because of habit, not because [music] it is the thing to do, because there is a person in your contact list who has stopped speaking over their future. >> [music] >> They have been so battered by what has not happened that they have stopped declaring what is coming. They have traded their prophetic voice for a resigned silence. And that silence is costing them the very future God wrote before they were born. Send them this word. It is not a message, it is a resurrection instrument, and you are the one carrying it to them. Now, open to Jeremiah chapter 29, verse 11. >> [music] >> "For I know the thoughts that I think toward you," said the Lord, "thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you an expected end." [music] Read it again, slowly. Every word is loaded. Now, I need to give you something that most preachers skip. The context because Jeremiah 29:11 without its context is a greeting card, but Jeremiah 29:11 inches is context is a weapon. When was this verse written? Not in a season of blessing, not at a moment of national victory. It was written to a people in captivity. The children of Israel had been from Jerusalem to Babylon. Babylon, the greatest empire of the ancient world. Foreign soil, foreign gods, foreign language, foreign food. Everything familiar had been stripped away. The temple was destroyed, the city was in ruins. The people were sitting by the rivers of Babylon, Psalm 137, weeping, [music] unable to sing the songs of Zion in a strange land. And into that moment, into the captivity, [music] the confusion, the grief, the disorientation, God speaks Jeremiah 29:11. This is not a verse for people who have everything going well. This is a verse for people in Babylon, for people in exile, for people who cannot see how the story ends from where they are standing. And if that is you today, if you are in a season that feels like Babylon, if everything familiar has been stripped and you are sitting by a strange waters weeping, then this verse was written specifically for you, not for the person in the blessing season, for you in this right now. [music] There are dimensions to this that the average believer has never accessed because most people quote verse 11 as a general comfort. >> [music] >> God says, "I know the plans I have for you. Everything will be fine." But that is not what the verse says. >> [music] >> Let us go deeper. For I know, the Hebrew word for know here is yada, >> [music] >> and yada is not casual knowledge. Yada is intimate, experiential, complete knowledge. It is the same word used in Genesis 4:1, "And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived." It is the knowledge of union, of deep personal interior access. God is not saying, "I am generally aware of plans that loosely relate to your life." He's saying, "I am intimately, completely, [music] personally acquainted with every thought I have toward you. I know them the way I know my own nature. >> [music] >> They are not filed away somewhere. They are active, they are current, they are burning in me right now." Psalm 139:17 and 18, "How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! How great is the sum of them! If I should count them, they are more in number than the sand, more than the sand." Every [music] grain of sand on every beach, on every continent. [singing] That is how many thoughts God has toward you. Not toward humanity generally, >> [music] >> toward you individually, specifically, by name. So when the enemy comes and says God has forgotten you, God has moved on from your situation, God is occupied with larger, more significant matters, >> [music] >> you answer with yada. He knows intimately, completely, [music] passionately. More thoughts toward you than grains of sand. He has not forgotten one of them. >> [music] >> "The thoughts that I think toward you," the Hebrew is makashava. It means thoughts, plans, purposes, [music] but also inventions, designs, constructions. God is an architect. He does not just generally wish you well. He has constructed a design. He has drawn blueprints. He has engineered your future with the precision of a master builder. Ephesians chapter 2:10, "For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God had before ordained that we should walk in them." Workmanship, the Greek is poiema, from which we get the English word poem. You are a poem God is writing. You are a master [music] work in progress. And a master does not abandon his poem in the middle of a difficult stanza. He works through the complexity to produce the beauty. Thoughts of peace and not of evil. Peace, shalom in Hebrew. And shalom is not the absence of trouble. Shalom means wholeness, completeness, nothing missing, nothing broken. It means every dimension of your existence functioning at its God-designed best. Spirit, [music] soul, body, family, finance, purpose, legacy, shalom. God's plan for you is total wholeness. Not partial blessing, not mostly good with some difficult areas. Shalom, complete, [music] comprehensive, lacking nothing, and not of evil. The Hebrew is raham, calamity, adversity, disaster. God is explicitly saying my plan for you does not include your destruction. My design for your life was never the poverty, was never the sickness, was never the prolonged delay, was never the broken relationship. Those things happened in the story, but they are not the plot God wrote. Thus saith the spirit of God. Stop reading the chapter you are in as if it is the end of the book. You are in a difficult chapter, but the author has already written the ending. And the ending is shalom. To give you an expected end. Expected end, the Hebrew is acharit, literally the latter end, the final outcome. And the word expected carries the meaning of hope, of anticipation, of a future held with confidence. God is saying your future is not uncertain. Your outcome is not up for debate. >> [music] >> The latter end of your story has already been written. And it is expected, it is a sure thing, not a speculation. Hear me, this is not theology, this is encounter. The enemy has been making your future feel uncertain. He has been making the outcome feel undecided. >> [music] >> He has been making you feel like the story could still end badly. But God says the end was written before the story started. And what God writes, he finishes. Philippians 1:6, [music] "He which had begun a good work in you will perform it until [music] the day of Jesus Christ." Will perform it. Not might, not probably, will. The one who started the work has committed to finishing it. Your future is not in the hands of your circumstances. It is in the hands of the one who holds your latter end. [music] Now, the second dimension of this word, and this is where the prophetic declaration enters. >> [music] >> Go to Romans chapter 4:17, "As it is written, I have made thee a father of many nations, before him whom he believed, even God, who quickeneth the dead, and calleth those things which be not as though they were." Calleth those things which be not as though they were. This is God's methodology. This is how he operates. He speaks things that do not yet exist in the natural realm as though they already do. >> [music] >> He told Abraham, "I have made thee a father of many nations." Present tense, already done. At the time he said it, Abraham had no children. He was nearly a hundred years old. Sarah was 90. And God spoke the future as present fact. This is not denial of reality. This is not positive thinking. This is not refusing to acknowledge what exists. This is speaking from a higher reality into a lower one. It is the language of the kingdom operating in the realm of time. [music] And God, when he created the world, did not pray about the darkness. He did not lament the void. He spoke. [music] Genesis 1 to 3, "And God said, 'Let there be light, and there was light.'" The speech [music] preceded the reality. The declaration created >> [music] >> the manifestation. And Genesis 1:26, God said, "Let us make man in our image after our likeness, in [music] his image." Which means the same creative power of spoken [music] declaration that was in God at creation was deposited into the being he created in his image. And you, you were built to speak futures [music] into existence. You were built to call those things which be not [music] as though they were. You were built to declare the machashava, the architectural designs of God over your own life with your own mouth until the invisible becomes visible. Until the spiritual becomes natural, until the future [music and singing] becomes present. I need you to stay with me because we're about to go somewhere [music] that will change the way you use your voice for the rest of your life. Ezekiel chapter 37, the valley of dry bones. God takes Ezekiel to a valley full of bones, very dry bones, dead a long time, no flesh, no sinew, no breath. And God asked, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And Ezekiel's answer is one of the wisest answers in scripture. He does not say yes because naturally they cannot. He does not say no because he knows who is asking the question. He says, "Oh Lord God, thou knowest." And [music] then God gives the instruction that carries the entire revelation. He says, "Prophecy upon these bones." Not pray about the bones, not believe in your heart about the bones, prophesy upon them. Speak [music] directly to them, address them, declare over them. Ezekiel 37:2-4, "Again he said unto me, 'Prophesy upon these bones and say unto them, "O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord."" >> [music] >> "O ye dry bones, hear the word of the Lord." The bones cannot hear with natural ears. Bones do not have ears. But Ezekiel was speaking from the spirit realm into the natural realm. He was addressing the potential, not the present condition. He was speaking to what they would become, not what they currently were. And what happened? Verses 7 through 10, there was a noise, a rattling, the bones came together. Bone to his bone, then sinew, then flesh, [music] then skin. And then God said, "Prophesy to the breath." And Ezekiel prophesied, and the breath came, and they stood, [music] an exceeding great army. From dry bones, a living army. From [music] impossible, inevitable. From death, life. Through the prophetic declaration, I decree and declare over every life under the sound of this voice, your valley of dry bones is about to hear the word of the Lord. The dead things are about to rattle. The scattered things are about to come together. The breath is about to enter, and what has been dead is about to become an army. Now, we declare, this is not the ordinary prayer section. This is the prophetic declaration altar. This is the place where we open our mouths and align our voice with the machashava of God, with the architectural designs he drew over our lives before we were born. I want you to do something specific. >> [music] >> I want you to speak out loud, not in your head, not as a thought, not as a wish, as a declaration, as someone who has the same image-bearing creative authority that God gave Adam in the garden, as someone standing in their valley of dry bones and choosing to prophesy. Father, we come before you on the basis of Jeremiah 29:2-11. We come on the basis of the yada, the intimate, passionate, [music] comprehensive knowledge you have of the machashava, the architectural plans, the designed future you hold over our lives. We come acknowledging that you wrote the ending before you started the story, and we come to align our mouths with what you wrote. We declare, your thoughts toward us are thoughts of shalom, wholeness, completeness, nothing missing, nothing broken. And we speak that shalom over every area of our lives right now. Shalom over our minds. We prophesy, the mind that has been in chaos receives order. The mind that has been in confusion receives clarity. The mind that has been in depression receives the oil of joy. Isaiah 61:2-3, "Beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning." I call it, I declare it, I speak it into existence. Sound mind, clear mind, peace-governed mind from this moment forward. Shalom over our bodies. We prophesy, every organ functions as God designed it. Every system operates in divine order. Every cell receives instruction from the [music] creator, not from disease. I call the body into alignment with the original design. >> [music] >> Isaiah 53:2-5, "By his stripes we are healed." Not will be. >> [music] >> Are healed. I speak it now. I declare it now. I call it into visible manifestation now. There is a man, I see him, he has been told his body will not recover. The doctors have used the word irreversible. He has been trying to accept it, but something in his spirit will not let him. That something is the machashava of God, the plan that was written before the diagnosis existed. The Lord says, "Irreversible is a medical word. It is not a kingdom word. In my vocabulary, the word is restored." I prophesy over that man, restoration, complete, confounding the medical record. The testimony is being written in his body today. [music] Shalom over our finances. We prophesy abundance, not lack, not barely enough, not survival. Deuteronomy 28:2-12, "The Lord shall [music] open unto thee his good treasure." The good treasure, the Lord's own treasury. I call it open over every life connected to this declaration. [music] The windows of heaven open. The gates of financial blessing open. >> [music] >> The spirit of poverty that has been occupying the financial space of our lives evicted. I call unexpected [music] income. I call divine connections that carry financial keys. [music] I call wisdom that produces wealth. Proverbs 8:18, "Riches and [music] honor, durable riches and righteousness." Not money alone, durable riches, wealth that sustains, wealth that carries purpose, wealth that funds the kingdom. There is a woman, I see her, she grew up in scarcity. Poverty was the only financial culture she ever knew. And even though she has education, she has gifts, she has worked, the ceiling has been low. The same level decade after decade. The Lord says, "The ceiling was not my design. It was a generational assignment, and I am breaking it today." I prophesy, you are the last generation in your bloodline to live under that ceiling. Your children are born into [music] a different financial inheritance because you received this word. I call [music] the ceiling broken by the spoken word, shalom over our families. We prophesy divine [music] order in our homes. Every family member connected to the lives of those under this voice, I call them by name before God. The spouse, the children, the parents, the siblings, the prodigal, the wanderer, the one who has gone far, I prophesy, none of them are outside the reach of the machashava of God. None of them have gone beyond the boundaries of the plans he wrote over their lives. >> [music] >> I call covenant marriages restored. I call broken father-child relationships healed. I call the prodigal back by the power of the sovereign mercy of God. Luke 15:20, "When he was yet a great way off, his father saw him." The father was watching, the father was waiting. And [music] when the son turned, the father ran. I prophesy, the fathers and mothers in this room who have been watching, you're about to run. Shalom over our destinies. We prophesy the expected end, the acharith, the God-confirmed latter end, the outcome that was written before the Babylon started. I call it arriving. Every door that was closed by the enemy, I prophesy it opens. Every opportunity that was stolen, I prophesy it is replaced with a better one. Every year the locust ate, Joel 2:25, I prophesy it is restored. >> [music] >> Every gift that was buried under delay, I prophesy, arise. Every calling that was dismissed as too small, I prophesy expand. >> [music] >> Every vision that was deferred until hope fell sick. Proverbs 13:12, I prophesy it is coming. There is a person under this voice who has been in Babylon for 7 years. 7 years of wondering why everything that should have moved has stayed still. 7 years of watching others advance while they waited. 7 years of praying the same prayer with increasing desperation. The Lord says the Babylon was not punishment. It was preparation. What I did in Joseph in 13 years of prison and pit, >> [music] >> I was doing in you in 7 years of waiting. And what Joseph stepped into when the preparation was complete [music] was so disproportionate to the suffering that the suffering became irrelevant. I prophesy [music] your Joseph moment is at the door. The Pharaoh is about to have a dream that only you can interpret. The promotion is coming from a direction you did not calculate. I call it now. Now, let us prophesy over the dry bones. >> [music] >> I want to name the dry bones that are in the valley of the lives connected to this prayer. And I want to speak to each one by name. Dry bone of dead hope, hear the word of the Lord. The hope that died from repeated disappointment, the expectation that went to sleep after the third unanswered prayer, the faith that was wounded by delayed promises. I prophesy live. Romans 4:18, Abraham against hope >> [music] >> believed in hope against the natural evidence, against the medical reality, against the logical conclusion, he believed. I call the dead hope back to life right now >> [clears throat] >> by the breath of the spirit of God. Dry bone of broken identity, hear the word of the Lord. Every person under this voice who does not know who they are anymore. >> [music] >> The failure redefined them, the betrayal relabeled them, the abuse rewrote the narrative of their value. They are living under a name the enemy gave them, not the name God wrote before they were born. I prophesy you are not what happened to you. You are not the sum of your worst moments. You are not the accumulation of other people's opinions about your worth. You are the machashava of God, his design workmanship. His poem, his poiema, [music] his master work. And the name he wrote over you before you were born. That is the only name that stand. [music] There is a young man, the name [singing] David comes to me. He has been living in the shadow of a father who never affirmed him. Every time he has tried [music] to step into his calling, he has heard the father's voice in his head. Not the words of encouragement, [music] the absence of them. The silence where praise should have been. The Lord says to David, I am your father. >> [music] >> And before you were born, before your earthly father could have had any opinion of you, I had already spoken. I had already written, I had already planned. And what I wrote is chosen, gifted, [music] sent, significant. I prophesy the voice of the absent father is [music] silenced. The voice of the heavenly father is amplified. Rise, David. The plans I have for you have not been canceled by his silence. Dry bone of silenced calling, hear the word of the Lord. >> [music] >> The calling that was spoken over you in a prayer meeting years ago and then went dormant. The gift that was burning and then the circumstances smothered the flame. The assignment that the enemy has been suppressing through distraction, through discouragement, through a thousand small decisions to put it off until later. I prophesy [music] awaken. Jeremiah 1:2-5, before I formed thee in the belly, I knew thee. And before thou camest forth out of the womb, [music] I sanctified thee. And I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. >> [music] >> The ordination happened before the birth. The calling was settled before the opposition started. And a calling that was settled before birth cannot be canceled by anything that happened after. I call the dormant gifting alive. I call the silenced voice restored. I call the defiant ministry released. Dry bone of barrenness, hear the word of the Lord. Every form of barrenness, natural and spiritual, the womb that has been empty, the ministry that has been fruitless, the business that has been producing nothing despite the labor, the prayers that seem to disappear without echo, I prophesy fruitfulness. John 15:16, ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you and ordained you that you should go and bring forth fruit and that your fruit should remain. Ordained to bring forth fruit. Ordained that it should remain. The barrenness is a season, the fruitfulness is the assignment. And I prophesy [music] the season is changing. There is a woman I see tears. She has been believing for a child for 5 years. She has undergone treatments, she has prayed, others have prayed over her. She brought herself to this word today because she's running out of the strength to keep hoping. The Lord says, I know the machashava I have toward you. And in those thoughts there is a child. I see the child. I have seen the child since before you were born. The child is in the plan. I prophesy life, life, life over that womb by the God of Sarah, by the God of Hannah, by the God of Elizabeth. The God who specializes in impossible pregnancies, >> [music] >> I call that child come forth. Dry bone of stolen time, hear the word of the Lord. The years that the locusts ate, the seasons that the enemy hijacked, the decade that felt wasted, >> [music] >> the decade of delay that looks like lost ground, I prophesy time restored. Joel 2:25, [music] I will restore to you the years that the locusts have eaten. Not approximate restoration, exact [music] restoration, not a consolation prize. The actual years. And the God who lives outside of time can restore what time took. What should have taken 10 years happening in one. What should have required three decades of building accelerated by supernatural favor, I call divine acceleration. The expected end arriving ahead of the expected schedule. Father, we thank you. We thank you because the machashava, the thoughts, the plans, the designs you have toward every person connected to this prayer are thoughts of shalom. They are not thoughts of abandonment. They are not thoughts of let us see how this turns out. They are designed thoughts, architectural thoughts, certain [music] thoughts written before the world began, unchanged by the Babylon, unaffected by the delay, unchanging. We have spoken what you wrote. We have called those things which be not as though they were. We have prophesied to our dry bones. And we wait now not in fear but in expectation for the rattling, for [music] the coming together, for the breath, for the exceeding great army that rises from what was dead. Shondai, tumbala ecclesia, reikai shondai ecclesia, tumbala reikai shondai ecclesia, tumbala reikai. The siege is over. The valley of dry bones just heard the word of the Lord. And heaven does not send the word without sending the breath. Even now in the spirit realm, there is a rattling. The scattered [music] things are coming together. Bone to his bone, sinew, flesh, skin. And the breath is entering. >> [music] >> What was dead in your life is not dead forever. What was dry is being saturated. What was scattered is being gathered. What was silent is finding its [music] voice. Walk into your favor. It has been waiting. The expected [music] end was always coming. The Babylon was a chapter, not the conclusion. And the God who knew you before you were born has never once revised the plan he wrote for you. Your destiny is preserved [music] by the blood. It was preserved through the captivity. It was preserved through the waiting. It was preserved through every season that tried to convince you it was [music] over. It is intact. It is whole. It is arriving. I decree this week is not ordinary. This week you carry [music] the prophetic declaration in your mouth. Every morning before the news, before the phone, you [music] open your mouth and you speak the machashava of God over your life. You call those things which be not [music] as though they were. You prophesy to your dry bones. You speak the future into the present. And things will begin to move. Things that have been stuck >> [music] >> will rattle. Things that have been scattered will align. Things that have been silent will begin to speak in your favor. From this altar you go as a prophetic voice over your own life. Not waiting for someone else to declare your future. You carry the blueprint. You carry the yada of God, the intimate knowing of the one who wrote your story. You carry the breath of the spirit that raises dry bones. And you carry the expected end, the God confirmed, blood secured already written acaris in your mouth, in your spirit, in your walk. Shondai ecclesia tumbala re kai shondai ecclesia tumbala shondai re kai [music] ecclesia tumbala shondai re. It is done. The declaration has been made. The dry bones have heard the word. The breath is entering and the expected [music] end is arriving. For I know the thoughts I think toward you, say the Lord, thoughts of shalom and not of evil to give you an expected end. It was written before you were born. It has not been changed and it is coming. Amen >> [music] >> and amen.
